# D8s

> Open-source tool for comparing Kubernetes resources across multiple environments.
> It diffs Deployments, ConfigMaps, Secrets, Services and more between any mix of
> clusters and namespaces, so you can find configuration drift between dev, staging
> and production. Runs locally against your own kubeconfig — no hosted service, no
> account, no data leaves your machine.

- Homepage: https://vamsinirala.github.io/d8s/
- Live demo (sample data, no install): https://vamsinirala.github.io/d8s/demo/
- Source: https://github.com/vamsinirala/d8s
- Downloads: https://github.com/vamsinirala/d8s/releases
- License: open source, free
- Requirements: Node.js 20+ and a working kubeconfig

## What problem it solves

Teams running the same application across several Kubernetes environments routinely
drift apart: production gets CPU and memory limits that staging never received, a
ConfigMap key is added in dev and forgotten everywhere else, an image tag lags a
release behind, or a Deployment references a Secret that no longer exists. These
differences are hard to see with `kubectl` alone because you end up diffing large
YAML documents by hand, one resource and one environment pair at a time.

D8s makes the comparison direct: define your environments once, then see every
resource across all of them side by side, with the specific fields that differ.

## Core concept

An **environment** is a `(kubeconfig context, namespace)` pair. That covers
dev/staging/prod as separate namespaces in one cluster, as entirely separate
clusters, or any mix of the two. Comparisons work across N environments at once,
not just two.

## Features

- **Multi-environment comparison** — for every resource kind, shows what exists in
  which environment and how many fields differ.
- **Field-level diff** — path-by-path comparison of a single resource across
  environments, filterable by probes, resource limits, environment variables,
  volumes, images and config data.
- **Image version drift report** — one table of every Deployment's container image
  tag across environments, distinguishing "versions differ" from "only deployed in
  one environment".
- **Deployment bundle view** — for a chosen Deployment, resolves everything it
  references (ConfigMaps, Secrets, PersistentVolumeClaims, ServiceAccount,
  PriorityClass) and everything referencing it back (Services, Ingresses,
  PodDisruptionBudgets, HorizontalPodAutoscalers), matched by label selector or
  scaleTargetRef. Flags dangling references pointing at resources that do not exist.
- **Side-by-side YAML diff** — the same comparison rendered in a Monaco diff editor.
- **Secret safety** — Secret values are hashed server-side before reaching the
  browser. You can tell that two Secrets differ, or that a key is missing, without
  ever seeing the contents.

## Resource kinds compared

Deployments, StatefulSets, DaemonSets, ConfigMaps, Secrets, Services,
PersistentVolumeClaims, Ingresses, PodDisruptionBudgets, HorizontalPodAutoscalers.

## How resource matching works

Resources are matched across environments by name. Names that embed the environment
(for example `payments-dev-app` versus `payments-prod-app`) are recognised as the
same logical resource via label-token stripping. An identical name appearing in two
environments always wins as an exact match before any stripping is applied.

Normalization removes fields that would otherwise produce false differences:
`status`, `managedFields`, `resourceVersion`, `uid`, `creationTimestamp`, and
rollout annotations such as `kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt`. Containers,
environment variables, ports and volume mounts are keyed by name rather than array
position, so reordering is not reported as a difference.

## Compatibility

Works with any cluster reachable from your kubeconfig — Amazon EKS, Google GKE,
Azure AKS, or self-managed — including exec-based auth plugins such as
`aws eks get-token` and `kubelogin`. D8s invokes whatever your kubeconfig already
specifies; it does not implement cluster authentication itself.

## Install and run

Download a release bundle, extract, and run:

```
tar -xzf d8s-<version>.tgz
cd d8s-<version>
./start.sh          # start.cmd on Windows
```

Or from source: `npm install && npm run dev`.

The release bundle contains the built application plus all runtime dependencies as
pure JavaScript, so a single archive runs on macOS, Linux and Windows. Only Node.js
20+ is required on the target machine.

## Architecture

A Fastify API server plus a React frontend. The server reads the local kubeconfig,
fetches live resources through the Kubernetes API, normalizes them, and computes
diffs. The frontend renders comparisons. Nothing is persisted to a database;
configured environments are stored in `~/.d8s/environments.json` on the local
machine.

## Comparable tools

Related tools in this space include helm-diff and helm-drift (Helm release drift),
kubediff and kube-compare (cluster versus reference config), and Monokle (manifest
IDE). D8s differs by focusing on N-way comparison across arbitrary
cluster/namespace environments with field-level output, rather than pairwise or
Helm-release-scoped comparison.
